newsitem.title: USA: Mich. debating $8.6 bln FY 1998 budget plans.
newsitem.headline: Mich. debating $8.6 bln FY 1998 budget plans.

text.p: Michigan lawmakers hope to complete work on an $8.585 billion general fund budget for fiscal 1998 before the Independence Day holiday, a spokeswoman for the state budget office said Wednesday.

Legislative leaders and representatives of Gov. John Engler agreed to target goals earlier this week that would set spending for all funds at about $31 billion, said Maureen McNulty, spokeswoman for the department of management and budget.
The major portion of the debate this week has been in trying to provide more than $2.85 billion for road repairs over the next five years, McNulty said.

The proposals include $570 million for repairs in the 1998 budget funded in part through a 4 cent-per-gallon gasoline tax hike that would generate about $200 million and federal reimbursements of about $200 million, McNulty said.

The proposals also include eliminating a diesel fuel subsidy to provide $28 million, eliminating spillage allowances for $15 million, increasing truck registration fees $38 million and making a $43 million appropriation from the general fund, McNulty said.
Engler has also announced plans for $18.2 million of bonds for fish hatchery renovations for fiscal 1998, McNulty said.
The legislature is expected to take up tax cut proposals in their fall session, McNulty added.
